answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks from independently anchored identities, so endorsements cannot amplify influence without limit. A sybil cluster behind a canyon-like sparse cut has low conductance: few edges leave relative to its volume, restricting walk flow into the cluster and bounding its aggregate voting weight by boundary flow and anchor mass. Dense internal links cannot open the vault; adding copper-colored identities alone does not increase trusted weight.
